title: Sequential shared engram codes with private edit fallback
hypothesis: Allocating a compact shared-basis code when projection residual <=0.02 and a private edit otherwise will preserve sequential memory retrieval while reducing total bytes versus storing every trace, with a lower fallback rate than native codebook growth.

world.sequence: 16 in-span memories followed by 8 out-of-span exception memories

development.tuning: none; fixed rank4 basis from first 8 examples and frozen relative residual threshold .02

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native fallback alias or quality/byte gate miss.

controls: shared code with no private fallback
Mirror code then private full-vector fallback
native low-rank code plus identical fallback
success_gate: PASS only if retrieval nRMSE <=0.02, specificity >=0.99, total bytes >=25% below independent and SERAC/GRACE controls, and Mirror strictly improves fallback rate or bytes over native low-rank fallback.
failure_gate: FAIL if quality/byte gate misses or native low-rank fallback exactly matches Mirror without advantage.
boundaries: Synthetic vector memory only; no AI Engram/SERAC/GRACE replication or cognitive claim.
The in-span then exception order is constructed; no natural fallback rate is inferred.
All private fallback vectors and keys are charged.
Fresh seeds remain sealed after native alias or gate miss.
